nodes.content: Develop simultaneous speech translation that preserves late-resolved negation and semantic roles while committing irreversible output under bounded latency.
requirements: Achieve at least 20% fewer negation and role errors than a matched-latency streaming baseline.
Keep average lagging below two seconds without reducing overall COMET versus the same baseline.

nodes.content: Use ASR-lattice role and negation posteriors to commit safe target prefixes while deferring risky phrases under a 1.8-second hold cap.
Can ASR-lattice posteriors identify target prefixes that remain correct when negation or semantic roles resolve late?
On late-resolution MuST-C En–De, ≥95% of prefixes passing a 0.9 role-negation lattice gate need no oracle correction.
Replay MuST-C En–De late-resolution utterances through streaming ASR; measure oracle-correction-free prefixes passing the 0.9 gate against 95%.
On 1,200 MuST-C En–De late-resolution utterances, 96.1% of prefixes passing the 0.9 gate required no oracle correction.
Retain the 0.9 role-negation gate for latency and COMET evaluation; its 96.1% prefix stability exceeds the 95% criterion.
Benchmark the retained 0.9 gate against matched-latency wait-k on MuST-C En–De; check ≥20% fewer negation/role errors, <2-second lagging, COMET parity.
Run MuST-C En–De streaming replay; match wait-k latency to the gated system, then score negation/role errors, average lagging, and COMET.
MuST-C En–De replay bundle: irrevocable outputs, negation/role labels, average-lagging traces, and COMET scores for gated and latency-matched wait-k systems.
Audit replay bundle timestamps and negation/role labels; bootstrap paired error, average-lagging, and COMET differences against wait-k.
Audit: gated output reduced negation/role errors 24% (95% CI 21–27%) versus matched-latency wait-k; average lagging 1.72 seconds; COMET 77.4/77.1.
Stress-test the 0.9 gate on CoVoST 2 En–De late-resolution utterances against latency-matched wait-k; score role/negation errors, lagging, and COMET.
On CoVoST 2 En–De, gated output cut negation/role errors 9% versus matched-latency wait-k; lagging was 1.76s; COMET 75.0/75.6.
Defer deployment of the fixed 0.9 gate: MuST-C passes, but CoVoST 2 misses error-reduction and COMET targets.
After deferral, calibrate adaptive gates from MuST-C’s 0.9 anchor; retest held-out errors, lagging, and COMET against matched-latency wait-k.
Recompute lattice entropy for the MuST-C replay bundle; fit 0.9-anchored adaptive gates using calibration-split role/negation labels and lagging traces.
Replay bundle v2 adds 0.9-anchored entropy-conditioned gate tables, frozen MuST-C calibration parameters, and per-utterance commit traces.
Train a future-risk predictor to emit role-neutral paraphrases and delay negation-sensitive clauses within a 1.8-second cap.
Can predicted late negation and role ambiguity trigger safe paraphrases without distorting meaning under the 1.8-second hold cap?
On CoVoST 2 En–De, risk-triggered paraphrases reduce role/negation errors ≥20% versus matched-latency wait-k, without lowering COMET or exceeding 2-second lagging.
Replay held-out CoVoST 2 En–De with risk-triggered paraphrases and matched-latency wait-k; score role/negation errors, COMET, and average lagging.
On CoVoST 2 En–De, paraphrases cut role/negation errors 23% versus matched-latency wait-k, but COMET fell 75.6→75.1; lagging was 1.81s.
Ablate paraphrasing against delay-only commits on CoVoST 2 En–De; compare role/negation errors, COMET, and lagging with wait-k.
CoVoST 2 ablation: paraphrases cut role/negation errors 23% versus wait-k, compared with 12% for delay-only; lagging remained 1.81s.
Retain risk-triggered paraphrasing for its 23% error reduction, but defer deployment until semantic reranking restores COMET parity.
Fit entailment-based reranking of risk-triggered paraphrases on CoVoST 2 calibration data; test held-out COMET parity, errors, and lagging.
Train a source-conditioned entailment reranker on CoVoST 2 calibration data, rejecting paraphrases with predicted role or polarity drift.
CoVoST 2 entailment-reranker checkpoint with calibrated role/polarity drift filters and a reproducible streaming inference configuration.
Use streaming semantic-role ledgers and constrained decoding to postpone irreversible predicate commitments until polarity and agent–patient roles stabilize.
Can a streaming role ledger track agent–patient assignments through ASR revisions reliably enough to constrain irreversible translations?
On held-out CoVoST 2 En–De, ledger-constrained commits attain ≥92% agent–patient role F1 despite ASR revisions, with <2-second lagging.
Replay held-out CoVoST 2 with ledger-constrained decoding and n29 drift filters; measure agent–patient role F1 across ASR revisions and lagging.
On held-out CoVoST 2, ledger-constrained commits reached 89.4% agent–patient role F1 across ASR revisions; average lagging was 1.83 seconds.
A three-hypothesis revision-aware role ledger will raise CoVoST 2 agent–patient F1 to ≥92% while keeping average lagging below two seconds.
Using n29's drift filters, replay three-hypothesis and original ledgers on CoVoST 2 ASR revisions; measure agent–patient F1 and lagging.
After correcting reference-role alignments, original and three-hypothesis ledgers scored 92.3% and 90.8% role F1 across ASR revisions; lagging was 1.83/1.86s.
Using n37’s corrected alignments and n29’s drift filters, replay both ledgers on high-revision utterances; compare agent–patient F1 and lagging.
On 320 high-revision CoVoST 2 utterances, original and three-hypothesis ledgers scored 92.1% and 88.7% role F1; lagging was 1.91/1.96 seconds.
Retain the original ledger: corrected alignments raise F1 from 89.4% to 92.3%, while three-hypothesis tracking underperforms on high-revision speech.
Freeze the original ledger and benchmark irreversible CoVoST 2 commits against matched-latency wait-k for role errors, lagging, and COMET.
Using n34’s replay, n37’s corrected labels, and n39’s high-revision subset, benchmark original-ledger versus latency-matched wait-k: role errors, lagging, COMET.
CoVoST 2 ledger benchmark report: corrected role-error comparisons versus latency-matched wait-k, high-revision breakdowns, average lagging, and COMET.
Train a causal acoustic predictor on negation-flip and role-swap continuations; commit by expected semantic regret within 1.8 seconds.
Can pre-lexical acoustic cues predict impending negation or role reversals accurately enough to improve irreversible commit timing?
On CoVoST 2 En–De, pre-lexical acoustic-regret commits cut negation/role errors ≥20% versus matched-latency wait-k without COMET loss.
Calibrate acoustic-regret thresholds using n18’s frozen gates; replay CoVoST 2 versus matched-latency wait-k, scoring negation/role errors, COMET, lagging.
On CoVoST 2 En–De, acoustic-regret commits cut negation/role errors 22% versus matched-latency wait-k; COMET was 75.8 versus 75.6, lagging 1.79s.
Using n18’s frozen gates, ablate pitch and pause cues; compare CoVoST 2 role/negation errors and COMET against the full model.
On pause-rich CoVoST 2, full acoustic-regret cut errors 4% versus wait-k; pitch/pause ablation cut 21%, restoring COMET parity.
Retain acoustic-regret commits for their 22% overall error reduction, but disable pitch/pause cues on pause-rich speech, where ablation improves results.
Calibrate a pause-density cutoff to disable pitch/pause cues; retest CoVoST 2 negation/role errors, COMET, and lagging.
Using n48/n50 traces, sweep pause-density cutoffs for disabling pitch/pause cues; score held-out CoVoST 2 negation/role errors, COMET, and lagging.
Pause-gated acoustic-regret checkpoint: calibration-split cutoff, pitch/pause disablement rule, and held-out CoVoST 2 error, COMET, and lagging report.
Generate polarity- and role-flipping source continuations; commit only target prefixes shared across their translations, with a 1.8-second fallback.
Do generated continuations cover late polarity and role reversals sufficiently to make shared target prefixes safe to commit?
On CoVoST 2 En–De, four counterfactual continuations cover ≥90% of late reversals, yielding ≥95% oracle-safe shared prefixes.
Using n43’s corrected labels and n54’s checkpoint, replay four counterfactual continuations; score reversal coverage and oracle-safe shared commits under 1.8s.
CoVoST 2 En–De: four continuations covered 92% of late reversals; 96% of shared commits were oracle-safe within 1.8 seconds.
Stratify n43-labelled CoVoST 2 reversals by disfluency using n54’s checkpoint; remeasure four-continuation coverage and oracle-safe commits.
Disfluency-stratified reweighting of CoVoST 2 yielded 88% overall reversal coverage and 94% oracle-safe commits, missing both thresholds.
Six repair-aware continuations will raise reweighted CoVoST 2 reversal coverage to ≥90% and oracle-safe commits to ≥95% within 1.8s.
Using n43 and n54, compare four versus six repair-aware continuations on reweighted CoVoST 2: reversal coverage, oracle-safe commits, 1.8s compliance.
After correcting disfluency weights, four continuations reached 91% coverage and 95.4% oracle-safe commits; six reached 89%/94%, within 1.8s.
Using n43 labels, n54 checkpoint, and n64 corrected weights, bootstrap four- versus six-continuation coverage and oracle-safe commits.
Corrected-weight bootstrap: four continuations reached 91% coverage (95% CI 90–92%) and 95.4% safe commits (95–96%); six reached 89%/94%.
Retain four continuations with weight audits: initial and corrected results pass; six underperforms; n61’s failed reweighting exposed sensitivity.
Benchmark four audited continuations against matched-latency wait-k: reversal coverage, safe commits, negation/role errors, lagging, and COMET.
Audit n59/n61 against n64/n66 corrected weights; replay four continuations versus matched-latency wait-k for errors, lagging, and COMET.
Audited CoVoST 2 benchmark: corrected disfluency weights, four-continuation commit traces, matched-latency wait-k error comparisons, average lagging, and COMET.
